DESCRIPTIVE WRITING STRATEGY My Broad strategy : I applied Q&A Format & Reverse Engineering Approach to tackle this If you understood these Two approaches effectively, your descriptive part is done and dusted.  PARADOX : Descriptive writing is Very Important But Overemphasised. How?  Here, I don’t mean to say it is not important. It has 200 marks in your Phase 2 RBI Grade B exam which is crucial in your selection.  What I mean by Overemphasised ? : if you start worrying about Descriptive Paper before you read, understand and revise your content from your notes & Start writing by beating around the bush, then you are overemphasising it.  Descriptive writing will come to you naturally if you have Basic notes ready with your Hand & Mind.  No of words to be written is also overemphasised in my opinion. RBI has given maximum words that can be written per question. 400 for 10 marker and 600 for 15 markers. But, it doesn’t mean you shall write closer to that word limit. Try to achieve around 75%. No hard and fast rule. All it depends upon the Question demand.  I personally wrote only 350 words in one 15 markers which is low. Not advisable as I did this due to paucity of time. However, I wrote a quality answer with lesser words. So i would like to emphasis that QUALITY MATTERS MORE THAN QUANTITY.  Try to reach 70%-80% of word limit. If you are not able to, finish it off with good quality.  I personally know some who’ve reached word limit in every question but couldn’t qualify. Also candidates who does the opposite have qualified. It doesn’t mean you should write less.  What you need to Prioritise ? : You need to prioritise to “EFFECTIVELY ADDRESS THE DEMAND OF THE QUESTION” asked rather to fret over the word count. If the question has two parts, your answer shall have

# Page 2^page=2
two parts divided equally. Once you addressed the demand of the question, move on to next question. This saves time and increase your marks.  Many start writing descriptive answer without even assimilating and consolidating everything into their mind. Why note making is Vital for Descriptive?  The moment you see the question on the computer screen, sufficient points shall flow from your mind.  You can write only if you have content flows from your mind. If you want content to flow from your mind, your mind needs to imbibe those content effectively. The only way for Me to do is to make SOLID EXAM READY NOTES & REVISING IT multiple times.  Exam ready notes mean? : Notes shall have everything that is needed & does not have anything more than what can be reproduced exactly on the day of exam. It shall have everything : quotes, data,facts, examples, intro and conclusion. Don’t leave anything on the day of the exam  ONCE you do the above, you can use rough sheet and scribble down all points roughly with an example while you give actual exam. Try to remember points through example. Let me break it down : Take every point seriously  Structure of Descriptive writing : Descriptive writing is there in ESI for 50 marks ; English in 100 marks ; Finance & Management in 50 marks  You will be given 6 questions out of which 4 questions has to be answered. 2 from 10 marks and 2 each from 15 markers.  Now the game is to write 400 words of 10 markers and 600 words for 15 markers within 90 mins  Try to give 25 mins each for 15 marker and 20 mins each for 10 markers. This shall be fixed in your mind. With these points in mind : what you shall do is to “Reverse engineering”.  If you have just 25 mins max for 15 markers, try to make notes in descriptive Q&A format.

# Page 3^page=3
 They have given you 600 words which is max. don’t try to reach 600 words. It is the maximum number of words given to you. Even space is counted towards number of words in IBPS software. So even if you effectively write 480-500 quality content rest will be taken care of.  Now you should realise that you shall prepare notes in Q&A format for descriptive writing only to write around 480-500 words. This will take care your descriptive writing in terms of content length.  I have prepared descriptive notes in Q&A format which I will share with you soon. HOW TO PREPARE NOTES FOR DESCRIPTIVE? Take one topic from syllabus. Say for example : Organisational change. Now when you see the topic, ask basic broad questions in your mind and prepare answers for that. For ex 1. What is organisational change? 2. What is the significance of this? 3. What are the resistance to organisational change? 4. How to overcome this organisational change?  Above questions will give you broad framework as to what questions that needs to be prepared.  Apply this framework for all topics mentioned in the syllabus.  Under each questions or subheading, take 5 points each with an example. Remember , The questions that you choose under each syllabus topic to prepare notes is THE MOST IMPORTANT part. Coz if you choose irrelevant questions, your answers, notes and entire preparation will be irrelevant. Questions in descriptive wont be complex. It is often simple. Like for ex : from the topic of “MULTICULTURALISM” : Positive and negative consequences of this was asked in 2025 PHASE 2 Exam. Like this, for every question : brainstorm

# Page 4^page=4
3 most important questions. Even 1 question is enough if the topic doesn’t have scope beyond that.  Don’t run behind complex questions in any platform. Don’t go to UPSC CSE Mains level. Not advisable till 2025 pattern.  For ex : In RBI Grade b 2025 Phase 2 : Finance paper : “How to strike a balance between Inflation and Growth through Monetary and Fiscal policies?” question was asked. See the Syllabus wording : “Striking a balance between Inflation and Growth through Monetary and Fiscal policies”  Thatz it. When a complex question comes, either you write based on what you’ve read from this approach or try to brainstorm on that day and do whatever you can. Nobody can chase behind complex questions.  If those kind of hard and complex questions asked, it is intentionally set to make you think on the day of exam and test you when you are unprepared. So control what you can but do it at your best How to write Descriptive answer?  Basics : You strictly need Intro, Body and Conclusion  Intro : Try to take an edge here. Don’t merely write Definition of Poverty : Instead, write “World bank defines Poverty as…….”. This is how you differentiates yourself from others. If possible, quote a data in intro itself. Thatz it  Body shall be in Point format. Ideally, Each point shall consists of subheading, a line and an example  Conclusion : summarise in one line. Give a futuristic outlook. Use some keywords like VUCA in management, Government slogan like “Sabkha saath, sabkha vikas..” etc for ESI, Recent RBI/SEBI initiatives in Finance. Think something along these lines.  If you look at my notes that I shared with you all, every answer structure has these components Now you know “How to write?”. Now Start preparing Notes based on these Demand

# Page 5^page=5
Next question that comes to your mind is : How you can prepare answers? : PRE-REQUISITE : Have Most probable Questions that could be asked in your Mind. I shared mine. Look at it. Now start preparing answers.  Use any one Paid course content supplemented with Artificial Intelligence tools like Gemini or ChatGPT. Give Questions & generate answers in a required format. Tweak the output based on your learning.  AI PROMPT TIP : Give it a Persona [shared on my channel @mintstreetmentor on Telegram ; New Tip : Instead of Usual Mode : Use “CANVAS” Mode in Gemini app to prepare Q&A for Descriptive. USE PRO VERSION if possible.  I Incorporated some from my handwritten with AI and made it organsied and structured. Go through my notes. Either use mine or prepare your own that shall look like that.  Number of points to be written 4-5 max with examples in each. If examples for each point seems overwhelming, increase the points but give examples to atleast 3 points without fail. Regarding typing speed :  You shall be able to write 10 marker each in 20 mins ; 15 markers each in 25 mins.  Your answer shall have all components I mentioned above. To do that : you need atleast 23 wpm required I guess. Solution : only through PRACTICE  Do practice on your laptop initially. Once your fingers get adapted to the Positional places of alphabets, try to buy an old type keyboard which is harder to press. Practice in that for a while.  On your Actual exam day : If your keyboard is not good, you shall ensure that it needs to be addressed. Inform supervisors/invigilators asap. While doing this, MAKE SURE you don’t login into your IBPS PORTAL. Once you do this, nothing can stop the Central server of IBPS from elapsing your time. So ensure your keyboard and mouse are safe before you enter login id and password. To do all this, go early especially for phase 2 RBI exam.
